1.title: Cut off one clear end plug
1.say: Pick up your cable and hold one clear plug end in your hand. Cut straight across the cable just below the clear plug with your cutters.
placements: one clear end plug with blue sleeve on network cable → cut off just below plug and set aside, either end works, keep the other clear plug on; in the video: blue cable on dark table, other end keeps its clear plug
cutting blades → closed straight across outer cable just below clear plug; in the video: cutter on brown table next to orange-handled tool
watch_for: if both ends have no plug you cut too much, one good clear plug must stay on the far end
if the cable is now very short you cut in the middle, cut just below the plug next time
1.check_yourself: It should look like a long blue cable with one clear plug still on one end and a flat cut end with no plug on the other.
1.safety: Keep your fingers clear of the blades and cut away from your hand.

2.title: Strip back the blue cover
2.say: Hold the cut end steady. Pinch the stripping tool around the blue cover about one inch from the end. Pull the cut piece off to show the small wires.
placements: outer blue cover of cut end → outer piece removed about one inch from tip to expose inner wires, tool pinched around cover then pulled off; in the video: blue cable held over brown table, black tool with yellow handles nearby
eight small inner wires → left sticking out of blue cover about one inch long; in the video: center of frame with colors visible
watch_for: if the small colored wires are nicked or cut you closed too tight, you should see eight whole wires
if you see less than one inch of wires you stripped too little and lining up will be hard
2.check_yourself: It should look like eight small colored wires sticking out about one inch from the end of the blue cover.
2.safety: Keep your fingers behind the blades and close the tool slowly.

3.title: Untwist and straighten small wires
3.say: Fan the eight small wires apart with your fingers. Untwist each pair all the way down. Pinch each wire and pull to straighten it.
placements: four twisted pairs inside cable → separated and untwisted all the way down to blue cover then pulled straight with fingers; in the video: held between both hands over brown table
thin white string filler → cut off at blue cover edge and removed; in the video: small white piece on brown table to the right
watch_for: if wires spring back together they are still twisted, they should lie apart flat with no curls
if a thin white string sticks out among wires you forgot to snip it off at the blue cover
3.check_yourself: It should look like eight separate straight wires fanned out from the blue cover with no twists.

4.title: Slide on the small cover
4.say: Pick up the small blue sleeve. Push the cut wire end through the narrow end of the sleeve. Slide it far down the cable out of your way.
placements: small blue sleeve cover → pushed over cut wire end narrow end first then slid far down outer blue cable below exposed wires; in the video: blue sleeve around blue cable below eight wires on brown table
watch_for: if the sleeve will not go over the wires you have it backwards, turn it around and try again
if the sleeve sits up by the wire tips it will get in the way, push it far down the cable
4.check_yourself: It should look like a small blue sleeve sitting loose around the blue cable well below the bare wires.

5.title: Line up wires green first order
5.say: Lay the wires flat left to right starting with white with green stripes then green. Continue with white with orange stripes then blue then white with blue stripes then orange. Finish with white with brown stripes then brown and snip the ends even.
placements: eight small wires → laid flat side by side left to right with tips pointing away in order white with green stripes then green then white with orange stripes then blue then white with blue stripes then orange then white with brown stripes then brown, ends snipped even straight across with cutters; in the video: blue cable held over fingertip, green striped wire on far left and brown on far right, orange-handled tool blurred behind
watch_for: if orange comes first on the left you made the other color code, the far left wire must be white with green stripes
if wire ends are jagged or uneven the plug will not seat, snip straight across so all tips line up
5.check_yourself: It should look like eight flat side by side wires starting with white with green stripes on the left and ending with brown on the right with even tips.
5.safety: Point the cutters away from your fingers when you snip.

6.title: Push wires into clear plug
6.say: Hold the clear plug with the gold pins up and the clip facing down. Push the flat wires straight into the back until they touch the front.
placements: flat ordered eight wires → pushed straight into back opening of clear plug until tips touch front clear wall under gold pins with blue outer cover tucked just inside back of plug, plug held with gold pins up and locking clip facing down; in the video: clear plug in fingers over brown table with colors visible through sides reaching front
watch_for: if wires stop halfway and blue cover hangs outside the plug you did not push far enough, tips must touch the front wall
if color order flipped left to right the plug was turned over, keep gold pins up and clip down while you push
6.check_yourself: It should look like a clear plug on the wire tips with colored lines reaching all the way to the front under the gold pins.

7.title: Squeeze plug tight with tool
7.say: Set the clear plug into the front slot of the squeezing tool. Squeeze the handles hard until it clicks then let go.
placements: clear plug with wires inside → set fully into front slot of plug squeezing tool with gold pins up and blue cable pointing out, handles squeezed hard until metal teeth flatten; in the video: black tool with orange handles on brown table, plug inserted from front
blue outer cover → pinched inside back of clear plug after squeeze; in the video: blue cover visible inside clear plug base
watch_for: if the plug pulls off with a light tug you did not squeeze hard enough, squeeze until you feel the click
if the blue outer cover sits outside the plug the wires will break, push cable in so cover sits inside before you squeeze
7.check_yourself: It should look like a clear plug pressed tight on the wires with the blue cover pinched inside the back of the plug.
7.safety: Keep your fingertips out of the jaws and squeeze with care.

8.title: Slide cover over the plug
8.say: Hold the finished plug in your left hand. Push the blue sleeve up over the back of the clear plug.
placements: small blue sleeve → pushed up along cable over back of clear plug until it covers the joint; in the video: blue sleeve snug over blue base of clear plug on finished blue cable end on brown table
watch_for: if the clear plug front is covered you pushed too far, only the back half should hide inside the sleeve
if the sleeve sits loose down the cable you did not push it up, slide it until it hugs the back of the plug
8.check_yourself: It should look like a blue sleeve pulled snug over the back of the clear plug on the finished end.
